newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold closes firmer on white metals.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold closes firmer on white metals.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended higher on Friday compared to New York's previous close, following tightness in platinum and palladium, dealers said.
Bullion closed at US$343.60/344.10 on Friday, against New York's US$343.10/60 close on Thursday.
Gold firmed steadily on the back of platinum and palladium, but strong selling interest at around $345 per ounce capped gains, dealers said.
"Actually gold is quite disappointing if you compare it to what's happening in silver and platinum," said one senior trader at a local bullion firm.
Spot platinum was quoted at $480 per ounce in early European trading, the highest level since 1990.
The Asian gold market on Friday repeatedly tested levels at $344.60 to $344.70 per ounce, but failed to break resistence, dealers said.
Gold was seen possibly trending slightly higher, still following the white metals.
